- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a “lagged mean reversion” rule: forecast should not drop below 1–2 days’ prior high.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.20) and forecast is trending, check for mean reversion bias — adjust downward if price has been rising for 5+ days.  
- In low-sentiment periods, forecast should not be overly optimistic — cap upward slope at 0.5–1.0% per day unless strong catalysts exist.  
- If true outcome diverges >10% from forecast in first 3–5 days, re-evaluate model’s horizon sensitivity — especially if sentiment is volatile.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid “flat plateau” behavior — if sentiment is weak, allow slight downward drift, not stagnation.
